The Open Door Notes were the 1899 and 1900 diplomatic circulars from U.S. Secretary of State John Hay to the powers with spheres of influence in China. They asked those powers to keep trade inside every sphere open on equal terms—the same tariffs, harbor dues, and railroad charges for all—and, in the 1900 note, to preserve China’s territorial and administrative integrity. Both offered descriptions miss that record: Hay argued for equal access and against partition, and the notes concerned trade in China rather than Chinese immigration to the United States.
